metadata.title: Limit Laws for Random Matrices and Free Products
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Non-commutative probability space
nodes.statement: A pair $(A, \varphi)$ where $A$ is a unital algebra over $\mathbb{C}$ (possibly non-commutative) endowed with a state $\varphi: A \to \mathbb{C}$ such that $\varphi(1) = 1$.
nodes.statement_clean: A unital algebra equipped with a unit-preserving linear functional, generalizing classical probability spaces.

nodes.name: Free family of subalgebras
nodes.statement: A family $1 \in A_i \subset A$ ($i \in I$) is free if $\varphi(a_1 \ldots a_n) = 0$ whenever $a_j \in A_{i(j)}$, $i(j) \neq i(j+1)$, and $\varphi(a_k) = 0$ for all $k$.
nodes.statement_clean: Subalgebras are free if alternating products of centered elements have zero expectation.

nodes.name: Free family of random variables
nodes.statement: A family of random variables $(f_i)_{i \in I}$ in $(A, \varphi)$ is called free if the family of subsets $(\{f_i\})_{i \in I}$ is free, i.e. the subalgebras generated by $\{1\} \cup \{f_i\}$ form a free family.
nodes.statement_clean: Random variables are free if the subalgebras they generate (with unit) form a free family.

nodes.name: Joint distribution of non-commutative random variables
nodes.statement: For $(f_i)_{i \in I}$ in $(A, \varphi)$, the joint distribution is the functional $\mu = \varphi \circ h: \mathbb{C}\langle\{X_i \mid i \in I\}\rangle \to \mathbb{C}$, where $h$ is the homomorphism with $h(X_i) = f_i$.
nodes.statement_clean: The joint distribution is the pullback of the state under the canonical homomorphism from the free algebra in indeterminates.

nodes.name: Limit distribution and asymptotic freeness
nodes.statement: Distributions $\mu_n$ converge to limit $\mu$ if $\lim_{n \to \infty} \mu_n(a) = \mu(a)$ for every $a \in \mathbb{C}\langle\{X_i\}\rangle$. Subsets are asymptotically free if their distributions converge to a limit $\mu$ and the family $((X_i)_{i \in I_s})_{s \in S}$ is free in $(\mathbb{C}\langle\{X_i\}\rangle, \mu)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Convergence of joint moments to a free limit distribution.

nodes.name: Additive and multiplicative free convolution
nodes.statement: For free $(f_1, f_2)$, $\mu_{f_1 + f_2} = \mu_{f_1} \boxplus \mu_{f_2}$ (additive free convolution) and $\mu_{f_1 f_2} = \mu_{f_1} \boxtimes \mu_{f_2}$ (multiplicative free convolution).
nodes.statement_clean: Free analogues of classical convolution operations on distributions.

nodes.name: Algebra of random $n \times n$ matrices
nodes.statement: $M_n = \mathcal{M}_n(L)$ where $L = \bigcap_{p \geq 1} L^p(\mathcal{S})$ over a probability space $(\mathcal{S}, d\sigma)$, with trace $\varphi_n(\sum a_{ij} e(i,j;n)) = \sum_{k} n^{-1} E(a_{kk})$.
nodes.statement_clean: The space of n-by-n matrices with random entries from L^p, equipped with the expected normalized trace.

nodes.name: Full Fock space and creation operators
nodes.statement: For an $n$-dim Hilbert space $H_n$ with basis $e_1, \ldots, e_n$, $\mathcal{F}(H_n) = \mathbb{C} 1 \oplus \bigoplus_{m \geq 1} H_n^{\otimes m}$. Left creation operators $\ell_j$ satisfy $\ell_j x = e_j \otimes x$, with $C^*$-algebra $\mathcal{E}_n$ generated by $\ell_1, \ldots, \ell_n$ and state $\varepsilon_n(X) = \langle X 1, 1\rangle$.
nodes.statement_clean: The full Fock space construction with left creation operators that realize free semicircular variables.

nodes.name: Standard family of independent unitary random matrices
nodes.statement: A family $V_j(n) \in M_n$ ($j \in J$) of unitary $n \times n$ random matrices whose joint distribution is the product of Haar measures on $U(n)^J$.
nodes.statement_clean: Independent unitary matrices each Haar-distributed on the unitary group.

nodes.name: Standard family of independent projection matrices
nodes.statement: A family $Q_j(n) \in M_n$ of self-adjoint projections with $\tau_n(Q_j(s)) = k_j/n$ a.s. and joint distribution given by the product of $U(n)$-invariant probability measures on the Grassmannians $G_{n,k_j}(\mathbb{C})$.
nodes.statement_clean: Independent uniformly random projections on Grassmannians.

nodes.name: Free Central Limit Theorem (semicircle law)
nodes.statement: If $(f_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ is a free family in $(A, \varphi)$ with $\varphi(f_n) = 0$, $\sup_n |\varphi(f_n^k)| < \infty$ and $\lim_{N \to \infty} N^{-1} \sum_{n=1}^N \varphi(f_n^2) = \alpha^2/4 > 0$, then $\lim_N \varphi(S_N^k) = \int t^k d\mu(t)$ for $S_N = N^{-1/2} \sum_{p=1}^N f_p$ and $d\mu$ the semicircle distribution on $[-\alpha, \alpha]$ with density $\frac{2}{\pi \alpha^2}(\alpha^2 - t^2)^{1/2}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Normalized sums of centered free random variables converge to the semicircle law.
conclusions: $\lim_N \varphi(S_N^k) = \int t^k d\mu(t)$ where $\mu$ is the semicircle distribution on $[-\alpha, \alpha]$

nodes.name: Free CLT under second-order freeness conditions
nodes.statement: Let $T_j$ be random variables in $(A, \varphi)$ ($\varphi$ trace) and $1 \in \mathcal{A} \subset A$ a subalgebra satisfying conditions $1^\circ$ (boundedness of mixed moments) and $2^\circ$ (vanishing of certain moments depending on the structure of multi-index $\alpha$). Then $X_{m,n} = n^{-1/2} \sum_{j \leq n} T_{\beta(m,j)}$ have asymptotically free semicircle limits with first and second moments $0$ and $1$.
nodes.statement_clean: Asymptotic freeness of normalized sums under structural moment conditions weaker than full freeness.
assumptions: $T_j$ random variables in trace probability space $(A, \varphi)$
conclusions: $X_{m,n}$ converge to semicircle laws with mean $0$, variance $1$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.1
nodes.statement: Three-step argument: (I) reduce to freeness assumptions; (II) reduce general case to free case via combinatorial counting; (III) prove the free case using Theorem 1.4 (free CLT).

nodes.name: Step I: Verify conditions $1^\circ$, $2^\circ$ from freeness
nodes.statement: Show that under freeness of $\{T_j\}$ and $\mathcal{A}$, both boundedness condition $1^\circ$ and moment-vanishing conditions $2^\circ$ a), b), c) hold, by polynomial expansion of $\varphi(T_{j_1} D_1 \ldots T_{j_k} D_k)$ in moments of $T_j$ and of products of $D_k$'s.

nodes.name: Step II: Reduce to free case via counting
nodes.statement: Expand $X_{m(1),n} D_1 \ldots X_{m(r),n} D_r$ as a sum of $n^{-r/2}$ scaled monomials and show that contributions from indices appearing more than twice vanish in the limit, reducing to counting pairings.

nodes.name: Step III: Prove the free case
nodes.statement: When $(\{T_j\}, \mathcal{A})$ is free, $(\{X_{m,n}\}, \mathcal{A})$ is also free, and existence of limit reduces to convergence of $\varphi(X_{m(j),n}^k)$, which follows from the free central limit theorem (Theorem 1.4).

nodes.name: Asymptotic freeness of self-adjoint Gaussian random matrices
nodes.statement: Let $Y(s,n) = \sum a(i,j;n,s) e(i,j;n) \in M_n$ be Hermitian random matrices with i.i.d. centered complex Gaussian entries normalized by $1/n$, and $(D(j,n))_{j \in \mathbb{N}}$ constant diagonal matrices with limit distribution. Then $(\{Y(s,n)\}_{s \in \mathbb{N}}, \{D(j,n) \mid j \in \mathbb{N}\})$ is asymptotically free as $n \to \infty$ with limit distributions of $Y(s,n)$ being semicircle laws.
nodes.statement_clean: Independent self-adjoint Gaussian matrices are asymptotically free, with semicircle marginal limits, and asymptotically free from constant diagonals.
assumptions: $(D(j,n))$ constant diagonal with bounded sup-norm and limit distribution
conclusions: Limit distribution of $Y(s,n)$ is the semicircle law

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.2
nodes.statement: Three-step argument: (I) bound mixed moments uniformly in $n$; (II) verify conditions $2^\circ$ a), b), c) of Theorem 2.1; (III) apply Theorem 2.1 via the symmetrization $k^{-1/2} \sum_{j \leq k} X_{\beta(s,j)}$.

nodes.name: Step I: Uniform boundedness of mixed moments
nodes.statement: Show $\sup_n |\varphi_n(Y(s_1,n) D(t_1,n) \ldots Y(s_m,n) D(t_m,n))| < \infty$ via combinatorial counting of pairings $\gamma$ of order $2$ without fixed points; the bound $\text{card}\,\mathcal{P}_n(\gamma) = O(n^{m/2+1})$ follows from connectivity of the associated graph quotient.

nodes.name: Step II: Verify condition $2^\circ$ c) of Theorem 2.1
nodes.statement: For $s_k \neq s_{k+1}$ ($k < m$), $s_m \neq s_1$ and admissible automorphism $\gamma$ of order $2$, show $\lim_n \varphi_n(Y(s_1,n) D(t_1,n) \ldots Y(s_m,n) D(t_m,n)) = 0$ by counting equivalence classes; conditions force $d(\gamma) \leq m/2$.

nodes.name: Step III: Apply Theorem 2.1
nodes.statement: Using injection $\beta: \mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ and Gaussian invariance, the joint distributions of $(X_s)_s$ and of $(k^{-1/2} \sum_{j \leq k} X_{\beta(s,j)})_s$ coincide; passing to $k \to \infty$ via Theorem 2.1 yields asymptotic freeness with semicircle marginals.

nodes.name: Asymptotic freeness for real symmetric Gaussian matrices
nodes.statement: For Hermitian/symmetric pair $Y(s,n), Z(s,n) \in M_n$ with $\text{Im}\,a = 0$, $\text{Re}\,b = 0$, $a(i,j) = a(j,i)$, $b(i,j) = -b(j,i)$, independent Gaussian entries, and $(D(j,n))$ constant diagonal with limit distribution: the family $(\{Y(s,n)\}, \{Z(s,n)\}, \{D(j,n)\})$ is asymptotically free with semicircle limit distributions.
nodes.statement_clean: Asymptotic freeness extension to symmetric and antisymmetric Gaussian matrix ensembles.
assumptions: $Z(s,n)$ purely imaginary anti-symmetric Gaussian with $E((b(i,j))^2) = -1/n$ off-diagonal
conclusions: Limit distributions of $Y(s,n), Z(s,n)$ are semicircle laws

nodes.name: Non-commutative limit law for Gaussian random matrices
nodes.statement: For $X_m(n) = \sum a(i,j;n,m) e(i,j;n)$ ($1 \leq m \leq M$) with independent Gaussian entries $E((\text{Re}\,a)^2) = E((\text{Im}\,a)^2) = 1/(2n)$, and any non-commutative polynomial $p$: $\varepsilon_{2M}(p(T_1, \ldots, T_M, T_1^*, \ldots, T_M^*)) = \lim_n \varphi_n(p(X_1(n), \ldots, X_M(n), X_1^*(n), \ldots, X_M^*(n)))$ where $T_j = \ell_{2j-1} + \ell_{2j}^* \in \mathcal{E}_{2M}$.
nodes.statement_clean: General (non-self-adjoint) Gaussian random matrices converge in *-distribution to free creation+annihilation operators on the full Fock space.
assumptions: Independent real and imaginary parts of entries

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3
nodes.statement: By Theorem 2.2, $X_m(n) + X_m^*(n)$ and $i(X_m(n) - X_m^*(n))$ form an asymptotically free $2M$-tuple with semicircle limits. A unitary $\mathcal{F}(\Omega)$ on the Fock space implements an automorphism of $\mathcal{E}_{2M}$ matching these limits to $T_j = \ell_{2j-1} + \ell_{2j}^*$.

nodes.name: Asymptotic freeness of independent Haar unitaries
nodes.statement: Let $V_j(n) \in M_n$ ($j \in J$) be a standard family of independent unitary $n \times n$ random matrices and $W(n)$ a constant unitary with limit distribution. Then $(\{W(n), W^*(n)\}, (\{V_j(n), V_j^*(n)\})_{j \in J})$ is asymptotically free as $n \to \infty$, and the limit distribution of $\{V_j, V_j^*\}$ is Haar measure on $\mathbb{T}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Independent Haar-distributed unitary matrices are asymptotically free from each other and from any constant matrix with limit distribution.
conclusions: $(\{W, W^*\}, (\{V_j, V_j^*\})_{j \in J})$ asymptotically free as $n \to \infty$
Limit distribution of $\{V_j, V_j^*\}$ is Haar measure on $\mathbb{T}$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.8
nodes.statement: Five-step argument constructing unitaries via the polar decomposition of Gaussian matrices, using approximation by polynomials in $X^*X$ and operator-norm tail bounds.

nodes.name: Step I: Polynomial approximation in $X^*X$
nodes.statement: There exists $C > 0$ such that if $|P(t) - f(t)| < \delta$ on $[0, C]$ and tail bound $d\sigma(\|X(n)\| > T) \leq \exp(-n T c_1)$ holds, then $\lim_n |X(n) P(X^*X) - X(n) f(X^*X)|_r < C\delta$ for $1 \leq r < \infty$.

nodes.name: Step II: Asymptotic freeness of $Y_j(n) = X_j(\varepsilon + X_j^* X_j)^{-1/2}$
nodes.statement: For $f(t) = (\varepsilon + t)^{-1/2}$ and $Z_j(n) = X_j(n) P(X_j^*(n) X_j(n))$, the family $(\{Z_j(n), Z_j^*(n)\}, \{W(n), W^*(n)\})$ is free; passing $\delta \to 0$ gives the same conclusion for $Y_j(n)$.

nodes.name: Step III: Approximate $U_j(n)$ by $Y_j(n)$
nodes.statement: For $U_j(n) = X_j(n)(X_j^*(n) X_j(n))^{-1/2}$ the unitary part of polar decomposition, given $\theta > 0$ there exists $\varepsilon_0$ such that $\lim_n |Y_j(n) - U_j(n)|_1 < \theta$, using spectral projection $Q(n)$ on $[0, \varepsilon^{1/4}]$.

nodes.name: Step IV: Asymptotic freeness of $U_j(n)$
nodes.statement: By passing $|R_1(n) - R_3(n)|_1 \leq d |U_j(n) - Y_j(n)|_1$ for monomials $q$ of degree $d$, the family $(\{U_j(n), U_j^*(n)\}, \{W(n), W^*(n)\})$ is asymptotically free.

nodes.name: Step V: $U_j(n)$ is a standard family
nodes.statement: Independence of $U_j(n)$ follows from independence of $X_j(n)$. Gaussian invariance under left unitary multiplication identifies the distribution as Haar measure on $U(n)^J$.

nodes.name: Concentration for Haar measure on free-group elements
nodes.statement: For $g = g_{i_1}^{k_1} \ldots g_{i_m}^{k_m} \in F_k$ a non-trivial element of the free group on $k$ generators with $i_j \neq i_{j+1}$, $k_j \neq 0$, $m \geq 1$, and $\varepsilon > 0$: $\lim_n \mu_n(D_n^\varepsilon(g)) = 1$ where $D_n^\varepsilon(g) = \{u \in U(n)^k : |\tau_n(u_{i_1}^{k_1} \ldots u_{i_m}^{k_m})| < \varepsilon\}$ and $\mu_n$ is normalized Haar measure on $U(n)^k$.
nodes.statement_clean: Words in independent Haar unitaries have asymptotically vanishing trace, with high probability under Haar measure.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.9
nodes.statement: Uses the Levy-family property of $(U(n)^k, \mu_n)$ from Gromov-Milman, eigenvalue estimates of the Casimir/Laplace operator on $U(n)$, and Lipschitz property of trace functions $f_n(u) = \sqrt{n} \tau_n(u_{i_1}^{k_1} \ldots u_{i_m}^{k_m})$.

nodes.name: Asymptotic freeness of independent Grassmannian projections
nodes.statement: Let $Q_j(n)$ ($j \in J$) be a standard family of independent self-adjoint $n \times n$ projections of dimensions $k_j(n)$ with $d_j = \lim_n k_j(n)/n$. Then $(Q_j(n))_{j \in J}$ is asymptotically free.
nodes.statement_clean: Random projections onto independent uniform subspaces of fixed asymptotic dimension fractions are asymptotically free.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.11
nodes.statement: Reduce to $Q_j(n) = U_j(n) D_j(n) U_j^*(n)$ via Theorem 3.8; further reduce to rational $d_j = p_j/q$ via approximation; use a constant unitary $D(n)$ with eigenvalues $e^{2\pi i p/q}$ and the fact that $(g_j d g_j^{-1})_{j \in J}$ generates a free product of copies of $\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z}$.

nodes.name: Fermionic analogue of Theorem 2.2
nodes.statement: Let $Y(s,n) = \sum a(i,j;n,s) \otimes e(i,j;n)$ in $(A \otimes \mathcal{M}_n, \varphi_n)$ where $b(p,q;n,s)$ ($p \leq q$) satisfy CAR: $\{b, b^*\} = 2/n$, $\{b, b\} = 0$, and appropriate definitions of $a$. Then with $(D(j,n))_{j \in \mathbb{N}}$ as before, $(\{Y(s,n)\}_s, \{D(j,n)\}_j)$ is asymptotically free as $n \to \infty$ with semicircle limit distributions.
nodes.statement_clean: The Gaussian asymptotic freeness theorem extends to fermionic random matrix entries satisfying anticommutation relations.
assumptions: $a(i,j;n,s)$ defined from $b$ via $i < j$, $i > j$, and diagonal symmetrization
conclusions: Limit distributions of $Y(s,n)$ are semicircle laws

nodes.name: Proof of fermionic theorem
nodes.statement: Three steps mirroring the proof of Theorem 2.2. Step I bounds mixed moments using $|a(i_1,j_1;n,s_1) \ldots a(i_m,j_m;n,s_m)\| \leq 1$; Steps II and III repeat the bosonic argument essentially verbatim.

nodes.name: Self-adjoint Gaussian matrices and Wigner's semicircle law
nodes.statement: Theorems 2.2 and 2.3 specialize to recover the well-known semicircle laws as limit distributions for complex self-adjoint matrices and real symmetric matrices with i.i.d. Gaussian entries (Wigner's law).

nodes.name: Free convolution computation: $X^*X D^* D$ limit distribution
nodes.statement: For Gaussian $X(n)$ and constant diagonal $D(n)$ with limit distribution $\nu$, the limit distribution of $Z^*(n) Z(n) = D^*(n) X^*(n) X(n) D(n)$ equals $\mu \boxtimes \nu$ where $\mu$ is the limit distribution of $X^*X$. The computation uses $S_\mu(z) = (1 + z)^{-1}$ via the Fock-space representation, recovering by free-convolution methods results obtained combinatorially in Wachter [16].

nodes.name: Rectangular Gaussian matrix (projection special case)
nodes.statement: When $D(n)$ is a projection with $\lim_n \varphi_n(D(n)) = \beta$, the rectangular $Z(n)$ with side ratio $\to \beta$ has $\psi_{\mu \boxtimes \nu}(z) = u$ satisfying $\frac{z(1+u)}{1 - z(1+u)} = u$, giving the Marchenko-Pastur-type formula $\psi_{\mu \boxtimes \nu}(z) = \frac{1 - z(\beta+1) + \sqrt{(z(1-\beta)-1)^2 - 4\beta z}}{2z}$.

nodes.name: Free group factor isomorphism
nodes.statement: The von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{R}$ generated by $T_j = \ell_{2j} + \ell_{2j}^*$ in $\mathcal{F}(H_{2M})$ is a type II$_1$-factor isomorphic to the II$_1$-factor of the free group on $2M$ generators; the vector $1$ is a cyclic and separating trace vector.

nodes.name: Real-orthogonal analogue of Theorem 3.8
nodes.statement: A similar result to Theorem 3.8 can be obtained in the real case (orthogonal random matrices) using Theorem 2.3.

nodes.name: S-transform identity for free multiplicative convolution
nodes.statement:
For probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}$ with first moment $

u} = S_\mu \cdot S_
u$.

nodes.name: Operator-norm tail bound for Gaussian matrices
nodes.statement: There exist constants $c_0, c_1 > 0$ such that $d\sigma(\{s : \|X(n)(s)\| > T\}) \leq \exp(-n T c_1)$ if $T \geq c_0$.

nodes.name: Levy-family property for $U(n)^k$
nodes.statement: $(U(n)^k, \mu_n)$ with the Hilbert-Schmidt-induced metric forms a Levy family; this follows from the Gromov-Milman isoperimetric inequality applied to the eigenvalue analysis of the Laplace operator on $U(n)$.
